sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Assessment of Abdominal Masses in Mid-Pregnancy
sections.description: Walks through the patient’s presentation, stabilization priorities, and targeted obstetric-gynecologic evaluation in the second trimester, highlighting symptom mechanisms and bedside findings that orient early reasoning.
subtopics: Key presenting symptoms: acute upper-left quadrant pain, pelvic pain, and dyspnoea—mechanical compression vs cardiopulmonary pathology
Vital signs and cardiopulmonary screen in pregnancy: normal oxygen saturation, ECG, and the importance of excluding pulmonary embolism or cardiomyopathy
Abdominal exam in pregnancy: size greater than dates, identification of a taut-elastic mass; recognizing limitations of palpation
Bimanual pelvic examination in pregnancy: detecting a fixed posterior pelvic mass; posterior fornix bulge and implications
Early symptom control while evaluating (analgesia, semi-orthostatic positioning for diaphragmatic relief)
Intercurrent issues: low-grade fever, UTI with Klebsiella pneumoniae; distinguishing infection-related signs from mass complications (torsion, necrosis)
Laboratory interpretation in pregnancy: physiologic leukocytosis and CRP changes vs true inflammation; iron-deficiency anemia vs dilutional anemia

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Workup in Pregnancy: Safe Imaging, Tumor Markers, and the Differential
sections.description: Details the stepwise imaging and laboratory approach that is safe in pregnancy, and how imaging characteristics and CA-125 trends refined the differential between adnexal and uterine pathologies.
subtopics: Ultrasound with color Doppler as first-line: two large unilocular cystic masses with peripheral vascularity; identifying a posterior intramural–subserosal myoma with cystic degeneration
Non-contrast MRI in pregnancy: safety (avoid gadolinium; prefer ≤1.5 T) and diagnostic value for large, multiple, posterior, or intramural lesions
MRI features in this case: thick-walled cysts, inhomogeneous T1/T2 fluid, focal T1–T2 hyperintense solid components; unclear cleavage plane with uterus for the caudal mass
Differential diagnosis: decidualized endometriomas vs cystic degenerating leiomyomas; how continuity with myometrium and vascular patterns guide attribution
Why pedunculated/subserosal fibroids mimic adnexal masses: anatomic displacement and absent visible stalk with gravid uterus (“steric bulk”)
Tumor markers in pregnancy: CA-125 physiology (first- and third-trimester mild peaks), limited specificity; cautious use of serial trends (36→41.8 U/mL) and integration with imaging
When to escalate beyond ultrasound: indications for MRI and limits of serum markers in obstetric decision-making

sections.section_title: From Indication to Incision: Multidisciplinary Decision-Making and Operative Strategy
sections.description: Explains why and how surgery was chosen in the second trimester, operative planning to protect the pregnancy, and intraoperative findings that changed management.
subtopics: Indications for surgery in pregnancy: refractory/worsening pain, restrictive dyspnoea from mass effect, risk of torsion/rupture/infection, diagnostic uncertainty, anticipated growth with uterine enlargement
Timing: rationale for second-trimester intervention when necessary (lower miscarriage risk vs third-trimester technical challenges)
Choosing surgical approach: reasons favoring laparotomy over laparoscopy for very large, highly vascular, and potentially intramural lesions
Obstetric safeguards: informed consent; fetal heart rate documentation before/during/after; minimizing uterine manipulation; brief operative time goals

Intraoperative steps and findings: peritoneal fluid sampling; confirmation of fetal cardiac activity; identification of a highly vascular pedunculated cystic leiomyoma with initial twist and leakage; myomectomy with double clamp; meticulous stalk hemostasis and uterine repair
Reason to leave the caudal mass in situ: fixed intramural–subserosal location, obstetric risk minimization, and expectant management plan
Adjuncts: progesterone prophylaxis (tocolysis strategy), antibiotic prophylaxis and culture-directed therapy for UTI, hemostasis considerations in gravid uterus

sections.section_title: Postoperative Care, Obstetric Follow-up, and Delivery Planning with Residual Myoma
sections.description: Covers maternal optimization after surgery, monitoring of pregnancy, and delivery strategy tailored to mass size and location, culminating in outcomes.
subtopics: Managing postoperative anemia in pregnancy: IV iron (ferric carboxymaltose) and transfusion thresholds; successful Hb/Hct recovery
Pathology correlation: benign leiomyoma with ischemic necrosis near twisted pedicle; negative cytology/microbiology of peritoneal fluid
Surveillance after myomectomy in pregnancy: serial ultrasound for fetal growth (86th percentile) and amniotic fluid; maternal symptom tracking
Delivery planning with residual pelvic myoma: anticipating cephalopelvic obstruction; decision for elective cesarean at 37 weeks on prior scar to minimize rupture risk
Maternal–neonatal outcomes: uncomplicated postpartum course, healthy neonate; partial postpartum regression of residual myoma and shared decision to defer further surgery
Antibiotic stewardship: tailoring to Klebsiella sensitivity; balancing maternal infection control with fetal safety

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology and Clinical Lessons: Leiomyomas in Pregnancy and How to Avoid Overtreatment
sections.description: Synthesizes mechanisms of leiomyoma behavior in pregnancy, why they mimic adnexal disease, evidence guiding intervention, and practical pearls for safe, conservative, and selective surgical care.
subtopics: Leiomyoma types and pregnancy physiology: growth kinetics across trimesters; degeneration patterns (cystic, red/ischemic) and pain/fever from torsion or necrosis
Mechanisms of dyspnoea and pain: mass effect on diaphragm and pelvis; inflammatory pain from degeneration
Imaging pearls: mapping number, size, location, and distance from the uterine cavity/placenta; when MRI adds value; typical vs atypical features of decidualized endometrioma vs fibroid degeneration
Serum markers caveats: CA-125 nonspecific elevations in pregnancy and benign gynecologic disease; role of serial trends and integration with imaging/clinical context

Risk–benefit framework: most masses managed conservatively; clear triggers for surgery (torsion, rupture, infection, intractable symptoms, oncologic concern); always aim to preserve pregnancy and avoid overtreatment

Surgical principles if intervention is needed: minimize uterine trauma/time, ensure hemostasis, consider approach by size/location, document fetal status, judicious use of tocolysis; leave non-obstructive intramural lesions in situ
Delivery considerations: how size, number, and location of myomas shape mode of delivery and timing; postpartum regression informing delayed definitive management
